details.description: Llama Guard 3 1B is Meta's compact content-safety classifier, fine-tuned from Llama 3.2 1B and distilled from the larger Llama Guard 3 8B, built to cut moderation deployment costs (including for mobile use) while classifying prompts and responses against the same 13-category MLCommons hazard taxonomy. Released September 25, 2024, it is meant to run alongside a chat model as an input/output guardrail rather than as a general-purpose assistant. It classifies content in 8 languages: English, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Portuguese, Spanish, and Thai, and Meta also publishes a pruned, quantized (INT4) build sized for on-device deployment.
advantages: Meta reports an English F1 of 0.899 with a 9.0% false positive rate on its internal test set, per the model card.
Meta reports the pruned, quantized (INT4) variant scores a higher 0.904 F1 with a lower 8.4% false positive rate on English, per the model card.
Distilled from the larger Llama Guard 3 8B, letting it run at a fraction of the compute cost, per the model card.
Meta publishes a pruned, quantized (INT4) build specifically sized for mobile deployment, per the model card.
Classifies content across 8 languages (English, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Portuguese, Spanish, Thai), per the model card.
disadvantages: Functions only as a safety classifier, not a general-purpose chat assistant.
Meta's own model card shows the larger Llama Guard 3 8B scoring higher F1 than this 1B model on most of the per-language benchmarks it reports.
Meta states hazard categories needing up-to-date factual knowledge may need supplementary moderation systems, per the model card.
Meta notes the model can be susceptible to adversarial and prompt-injection attacks, per the model card.
use_cases: Screening user prompts before they reach a language model, at lower compute cost than Llama Guard 3 8B.
Screening model responses before they reach a user.
On-device or mobile content moderation using the pruned INT4 build.

notes: Catalog's max_input/max_output_tokens (131072) match the 131K context window Meta and Fireworks AI report for this Llama-3.2-1B-based model, so no conflict. Meta's model card does not say whether its per-language F1/FPR table is prompt classification, response classification, or a combined metric, so the evaluation entry is left unlabeled by task rather than guessed. F1 is Meta's own 0-1 metric, multiplied by 100 here to fit the catalog's 0-100 convention.
